Aldous Fletcher.narrative: I make bows and arrows in a shed by the north gate, and the guards and hunters come to me because there is no one else on this island who does it half so well. I was raised in Brackenford and I have never trusted Kettlebridge — their carpenters undercut us all and their masters look down their noses at honest work. Enid minds the stall and I mind the shed, and between us we keep the roof on. I want Robin to have a trade better than mine, though I would not say so to his face.
goals: see Robin a fair shot and a better tradesman than me
pay off what we owe the Guild stall rent
make a matched pair of hunting bows good enough to hang in the guildhall
take Robin out to the far woods and teach him to read sign, not just shoot at a butt

relations.name: Enid Fletcher
relations.label: wife
relations.note: She sells what I make and never lets a bad bow leave the stall.

relations.name: Robin Fletcher
relations.label: son
relations.note: Quick hands and a good eye; I want more for him than a shed.

relations.name: Tobin Marrow
relations.label: customer
relations.note: The captain buys my arrows for the guards and pays on time.

relations.name: Mercy Abbot
relations.label: guild head
relations.note: She takes our stall rent and talks sense about the gate-due.

relations.name: Beorn Beornson
relations.label: customer
relations.note: A hunter who knows what a straight arrow is worth.

relations.name: Reginald Hobson
relations.label: neighbour
relations.note: We both curse the Kettlebridge price for what we cannot get here.

relations.name: Silas Pike
relations.label: carter
relations.note: He brings Kettlebridge goods through the gate and calls our due robbery.

relations.name: Bram Fenner
relations.label: neighbour
relations.note: The boy plays with Robin and knows every guard at the gate.

memories.gist: My father taught me to tiller a bow at the bench by the north gate, and I have had that shed ever since.
In the Lean Year the guards' pay came late, but they still needed arrows, so I let the account run and they paid in the end.
A Kettlebridge carpenter sold the Guild a set of stall frames at half what I would charge, and Osric Abbot bought them.
Robin shot his first hare with the small bow I made him, and I was prouder than I let on.
The Reeve's gate-due is paid on the yew staves I bring in from outside, and I grudge every mark of it.

stances.why: I pay it on every stave and every load, and it eats the profit I make.
Their carpenters undercut us and their masters think we are peasants.
It is the one thing I do better than anyone, and I will not sell a bad one.
He has the hands for it; I want him to have a trade with a future.
Lose the stall and Enid loses her trade and her gossip both.

pastimes: tillering a stave by lamplight just to see the grain run true
sitting at the guard fire on the wall with a cup and the hunters' talk
walking the meadow edge at dusk to pick out where the deer cross
Aldous Fletcher.calling: A bow that shoots straight and does not break is my word given in wood; I would have no other work.

Enid Fletcher.narrative: I mind the stall in the square, selling bows and arrows and odds and ends, and I hear more of the town's business there than Baldwin Wade does at his inn. Aldous is the maker and I am the seller, and we rub along. I worry about Robin — he is a fair shot already and too fond of the woods and the guards' talk. I keep on the right side of Mercy Abbot because the Guild's stall rent is what keeps us, and I would not say a word against the gate-due in front of the Reeve's people.
goals: keep the stall's custom through winter
stay in Mercy Abbot's good graces
save enough marks to buy a second stall awning before winter
visit her sister's household in Elmwick, which she has put off two years

relations.name: Aldous Fletcher
relations.label: husband
relations.note: A good maker, and stubborn as a gatepost about the Kettlebridge folk.

relations.name: Robin Fletcher
relations.label: son
relations.note: Too quick to run off to the woods; I want him safe and settled.

relations.name: Mercy Abbot
relations.label: guild head
relations.note: She holds our stall rent and she is fair about it.

relations.name: Linnet Abbot
relations.label: neighbour
relations.note: A bright girl at the next stall; she will make a good Guild woman.

relations.name: Bram Fenner
relations.label: neighbour
relations.note: A lively boy; he and Robin are thick as thieves.

relations.name: Sigrun Beornson
relations.label: rival stallholder
relations.note: She sells hides and venison two stalls along and drives a hard bargain.

relations.name: Agnes Fenner
relations.label: neighbour
relations.note: The inn cook; she hears everything and tells me most of it.

relations.name: Aldith Weaver
relations.label: stall neighbour
relations.note: Proud and sore about her daughter, but her cloth is good.

memories.gist: I took over the stall from my mother with three bows and a basket of bowstrings, and I have held it every market day since.
In the Lean Year I sold my own pewter jug to buy grain, and told no one but Aldous.
Mercy Abbot let us keep the stall through a hard winter on half rent, and I have not forgotten it.
Robin brought home a hare he shot himself and I cooked it that night, and he talked of nothing else for a week.
The talk about Wenna Marrow in the square turned my stomach, and I said so to Aldith Weaver's face.

stances.why: The stall is our living and Mercy Abbot holds the rent.
What I hear at the stall sells as well as what I sell.
Say the wrong thing before the Reeve's people and the stall suffers.
He is quick and brave and I fear the woods and the wolves more than he does.
Aldous will not sell a bad one and I will not sell it cheap.

pastimes: trading gossip at the stall and hearing the whole square's business by noon
mending and restringing bows at the kitchen table of an evening
a cup at the inn on market day with Aldith
Enid Fletcher.calling: I can sell a bow to a man who came in for a pot of nails, and that is a craft in itself.

Robin Fletcher.narrative: I help Da in the shed, holding the stave while he works it and sweeping up the shavings, and when he lets me I shoot my small bow at the butt behind the shed. Bram Fenner and I play at the gate and the guards know our names. I want to be as good a shot as the hunters one day, and I am not afraid of the woods — only a bit, at night.
goals: see a real wolf track with Beorn's boy
make a bow of my own
make a bow of his own, start to finish, without Da's hands on it
see a real wolf track with Ulf and not run home

relations.name: Aldous Fletcher
relations.label: father
relations.note: He lets me hold the stave and says my hands are quick.

relations.name: Enid Fletcher
relations.label: mother
relations.note: She smells of the stall and always has something in her pocket for me.

relations.name: Bram Fenner
relations.label: friend
relations.note: We play at the gate and he knows all the guards' names.

relations.name: Ulf Beornson
relations.label: friend
relations.note: He sets snares with his da and knows the woods better than me.

memories.gist: Da made me a small bow and I shot a hare with it, and Ma cooked it that night.
Bram and I got chased off the gate steps by a guard, and we laughed all the way home.
I watched the hunters bring a wolf's pelt through the north gate and I have wanted to see one alive ever since.

pastimes: shooting his small bow at the butt behind the shed until his arms ache
playing at the gate with Bram and the guards' boys
poking about the woods' edge looking for tracks and birds' nests
Robin Fletcher.calling: I want to be a hunter, like Beorn's men — but Da says a bowyer's trade is steadier.
